page: Amazon Web Services c8g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs using the AWS Neoverse-V2 CPU model from the ARMv9 family. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing the instance in the top 25% and top 10% respectively. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, achieving top-tier status in both large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests. This high memory throughput is reflected in top-tier Passmark memory and database operation scores. Single-core performance, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics, falls within the average range. The instance also demonstrates top-tier performance in static web serving throughput and software compilation tasks.

The c8g.12xlarge offers high cost-efficiency relative to its compute density, leveraging the ARM64 architecture to deliver high multi-threaded performance per resource unit. However, workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or local NVMe storage may face limitations, as the instance lacks local storage and exhibits average single-core benchmark results. The dedicated, non-hyperthreaded core allocation ensures predictable execution. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
